design.summary:
ENGINE-ONLY design for plan v5 step B, the commit contract. Nothing in the repository was edited, committed or run. Experiments ran in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-dadleet-src-skill-craft/f24838dd-d5f5-44a8-854e-3d9ddea18aed/scratchpad/b1012/exp (prototype of the new parser proto/shiploop_lessons.py, 159 lines; proto/shiploop_git.py; scan, byte-count and git scripts). That tree should be exported compactly into docs/experiments/commit-contract-engine-<date>/ with the journal entry (owner rule: evidence lives in the repo).

DESIGN IN SIX POINTS
1. One new pure leaf module, skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_lessons.py (stdlib only, imports nothing from ShipLoop), owns the commit-message grammar: lessons sections, the Remote change section, Learned-from lines. knowledge_home._sections is deleted; learnings() reads outcome.md through it. The harness imports the same module.
2. shiploop_git stays the one commit path and gains: --cleanup=whitespace on every commit; an empty commit that uses --allow-empty --only and honours message_file; a message that may be a callable of the paths actually committed; resolve_commit / resolve_citations (git resolves SHAs, never the model); messages_since.
3. _improve_commit: existing file checks, then nothing-to-commit (D4, never asks for lessons), then (empty-delta only) already-recorded, then lessons, citations, credentials, then commit. A Remote change section with nothing pending makes a commit with no files. Citation prefixes are rewritten to full IDs in place. No trailers, no schema, no state-version change.
4. Bypass without packet text (35% of Improve-window commits): (a) commit_refusal, which today literally tells the model to run a raw git commit, now names the improve-commit command; (b) improve-commit's command and message rules are written into parent-return.md, a file the frozen contract already lists as a resource; (c) the frozen authority says the child runs no callback EXCEPT improve-commit and points at that file (+102 bytes, ladder +134/+31/0); (d) improve-complete prints a counted NOTICE for commits made since the bind that carry no lessons section (bind snapshot gains a head key). Nothing blocks.
5. Script-built bodies: knowledge commits carry "Result (<stage>):" plus the accepted summary verbatim; release-verify keeps its outcome.md sections first (bytes unchanged); the item commit keeps the integrate summary and gains a Learned: block harvested from earlier same-item summaries; the leftovers commit names its files. A summary is a RECORD, not a lesson: it is never labelled Learned. Lessons appear only where a model wrote a recognised label.
6. Honest expectations from saved data: the new grammar reads 72 of 384 commits in 34 saved work repos, including all 42 Improve-style commits (5 of them only because of the one-paragraph inline form). Regrading by subject: 292 script commits of which 26 carry lessons (release-verify only), 67 non-script commits by a script identity of which 44 do, 25 model-typed of which 2 do. Only 2 of 1,223 accepted-stage summaries contain a lessons label (both carry-forward "Lessons:"), so until fork-owned packet text asks for it, script commits will carry records but almost no new lessons.

FINDINGS THE PLAN DID NOT HAVE
- DEFAULT_COMMIT_AUTHORITY in test/shiploop-actual-improve-cli.test.py and test/shiploop-full-runtime.test.py are hand-written authority strings of fixture contracts; nothing derives them from improve_start_contract, so the plan's "update the DEFAULT_COMMIT_AUTHORITY pins" is not needed. The only pin on the engine's authority text is the substring "No push or merge" (actual-improve-cli, in test_improve_start_freezes_the_contract_and_starts_the_runtime).
- The empty-commit path through improve-commit is reachable only from stages that run an Improve child (spec, test-strategy, plan, step-plan, test-spec, carry-forward last item, system-test-author, release-plan). release, release-verify and operations have none, so a deploy at release cannot be recorded this way. A stage-level path (same grammar inside the stage summary) is the smallest next step and stays deferred.
- Improve children all run before the workspace return, so follow_up_knowledge_return needs no change now.
- Real one-paragraph Improve messages exist (4 of 5 in the newest saved run restate their Changes text under Key learnings): the gate checks presence, never substance.
design.lessons_grammar:
GRAMMAR (reference implementation: proto/shiploop_lessons.py in the scratchpad exp dir; it is what the module should contain).

A section is a label plus a body. Labels are matched without regard to case. Four forms are accepted:
1. heading: a line  ^#{1,3}[ \t]+LABEL[ \t]*:?[ \t]*$  (for example "## Key learnings"). Body runs to the next markdown heading of any level 1-3; blank lines are allowed inside. This is exactly the rule knowledge_home.learnings() uses for outcome.md today.
2. colon: a line starting LABEL[ \t]*:  followed by text on the same line and/or the lines after it. Body = rest of the line plus following lines up to a blank line, a heading, a code fence, or a line that is itself a label (^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z-]*( [A-Za-z-]+){0,3}:(\s|$), which stops at "Remaining work:", "Co-Authored-By:", "Learned-from:").
3. bare: a line that is only the label (release-verify's existing body uses "Learned", "Key considerations", "Open for the next run" this way). Body as in form 2.
4. inline: the label after a sentence end ([.;!?)\]]\s+LABEL:) inside a line of a one-paragraph message. Body = rest of that line up to the next " Capitalised label:" or the end of the line. One line only.

LESSON LABELS (why each): "Key learnings" (the Improve card's own label: 38 colon + 5 inline saved commits), "Key learning" (3 saved commits), "Lessons learned" (the owner's phrase; a model told "lessons learned" will write it), "Lessons" (carry-forward summaries in 8 saved runs open with "Lessons:"; the improve-complete --notes text is called lessons), "Learned" (release-verify's bare form: 26 saved commits). NOT lesson labels: "Key considerations" and "Open for the next run" (decisions and follow-ups; knowledge_home.LEARNING_SECTIONS keeps them for outcome.md), "Learned-from" (the citation key; the hyphen keeps it out of the colon/bare patterns structurally), and prose such as "We learned: x".

NON-EMPTY RULE: a section counts only if its body holds at least one letter or digit (a lone "-" or "..." is not a lesson). The script cannot judge truth or usefulness; "Key learnings: none new beyond commit d171177ac28b" (a real saved checkers-1 commit) counts, and so would a restatement of Changes (4 of 5 in the saved battleship-1 one-paragraph commits). That is measured, never refused (no word list, no thresholds).

NOT ACCEPTED (and why that is cheap): a bulleted label ("- Key learnings: x"), a bold label ("**Key learnings:** x"), an indented label, a label inside a fenced code block, a heading of four or more # (a refusal names the accepted forms and one such commit costs one turn). Probe over the 72 saved commits that carry a lessons section: all use forms 2, 3 or 4; none uses a bullet, bold, indent or deep heading.

REMOTE CHANGE: label "Remote change", forms 1-3 only (no inline); body must be non-empty. Asked content (packet/refusal text, not checked): system alias, what changed, where its evidence is, no secrets.

LEARNED-FROM: a line (case-insensitive key, line start only, not in a fence)  Learned-from: <token> <contribution>. Token = 7 to 64 hex digits ({7,64} covers SHA-256 repositories). The contribution must be on the same line. A citation inside a one-paragraph message is not a Learned-from line and is not validated (free text stays free).

EVIDENCE (scan_forms.py, run_proto.py, baseline.py over /Users/dadleet/e2e-runs/*/*/work, 34 repos, 384 commits): lessons section found in 72 commits; by form: colon "Key learnings" 38, colon "Key learning" 3, inline "Key learnings" 5, bare "Learned" 26. Of 42 Improve-style commits (Review: and Plan: present) all 42 pass; without the inline form 5 would be refused (all from 20261010/battleship-1, which writes every label in one paragraph). Edge probe results: heading, heading with colon, colon inline, colon then bullets on the next line, colon then prose on the next line, bare, singular, UPPERCASE, label then Learned-from (the section stops before it) are read; empty colon, "Key learnings: -", Learned-from alone, "We learned: x", bulleted, bold, fenced, indented are not.

ACCEPTED-STAGE SUMMARIES (scan_states.py): 2 of 1,223 history rows contain a recognised lessons section (both carry-forward, "Lessons:"); summary length median 302, p95 951, max 2,502 characters. improve-complete --notes text (receipt.lessons) exists in 20 of 205 saved Improve results, median 389 characters; it is a successor handoff more than a lesson and is NOT harvested (see unknowns).
design.parser_owner:
Owner: a NEW leaf module skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_lessons.py, standard library only, imports nothing from ShipLoop. knowledge_home._sections (private, one caller: learnings()) is deleted; learnings() builds its dict from lessons.sections(text, LEARNING_SECTIONS), so there is one heading-and-label parser (S-12). The heading-body rule is one helper inside the module.

Public surface (signatures):
- LESSON_LABELS = ("Key learnings", "Key learning", "Lessons learned", "Lessons", "Learned"); REMOTE_LABEL = "Remote change"
- class Section(label, form, line, body); sections(text, labels) -> list[Section]
- has_content(body) -> bool; lessons(text) -> str ('' when none); remote_change(text) -> str
- class Citation(line, token, contribution); citations(text) -> list[Citation]; with_full_ids(text, resolved: Mapping[int, str]) -> str

Import graph (no cycle): shiploop_lessons <- shiploop_git (resolve_citations needs citations and with_full_ids) <- shiploop_knowledge_home, shiploop_item_scope, shiploop_workspace, shiploop_navigator. shiploop_lessons <- shiploop_improve_changes (also imports shiploop_git, which does not import it back) and <- shiploop_navigator. shiploop_privacy stays below shiploop_git as today. git-touching helpers live in shiploop_git, parsing in shiploop_lessons; nothing in the leaf module runs git.

Harness (task H): test/shiploop_e2e/run.py and progress.py already put skills/shiploop/scripts on sys.path before importing shiploop modules. metrics.py does NOT, and progress.py imports metrics before it inserts the path, so a top-level "import shiploop_lessons" in metrics.py would raise ImportError from progress.py. Either compute metrics.commits in run.py and pass the parser results in, or import inside the function after a local sys.path insert. Counters then use lessons.lessons(msg), lessons.citations(msg) and lessons.sections(msg, ...) so the harness and the engine can never disagree about what counts.
design.improve_commit_checks:
ORDER in _improve_commit(core, root, state, args), with the exact refusal text. NavigatorError prints as "ShipLoop navigator: <message>" plus two fixed lines, so line 1 of each message below is the fix and the exact command. cmd = _callback(core, root, "improve-commit", action=action_id, message=str(message_path)); mp = str(improve_commit_message_path(child)).

Unchanged first checks (text extended to restate the command; the substring pinned by the existing test stays): bound child; message path equals the printed one -> "the commit message must be the printed file {mp}; run: {cmd}"; file exists -> "write the commit message with a file tool first: {mp}, then run: {cmd}"; non-empty -> "the commit message file is empty: write the message to {mp} with a file tool (it needs a \"Key learnings:\" line), then run: {cmd}"; changes = improve_changes.review_changes(...) not None (unchanged).

Then, in order:
1. NOTHING TO COMMIT (D4). pending = changes[1]; remote = lessons.remote_change(message). If not pending and not remote: print the unchanged "Nothing to commit: every file this review changed is already committed (...)." / "; the review changed no file." and return 0. Never asks for lessons. A Remote change label with an empty body counts as absent.
1a. ALREADY RECORDED (empty-delta only). If not pending and remote: recorded = [id for id, text in improve_changes.window_commits(root, repo, action_id) or [] if same(lessons.remote_change(text), remote)] where same() compares whitespace-collapsed text. If recorded: print "Nothing to commit: this remote change is already recorded in {id12}; continue the review or run improve-complete when the loop is done." and return 0 (a benign no-op, so a re-run after a context loss cannot make a second commit and costs no refusal). With no recorded bind head the guard is skipped (unknown).
2. LESSONS (only reached when a commit will be made: pending files, or an empty remote-change commit). If not lessons.lessons(message):
 line 1: Add a "Key learnings:" line to {mp} saying what this iteration taught that a later iteration or run should reuse, then run: {cmd}
 line 2: ShipLoop commits a review's changes only with a lessons section, because the commit message is what the next run reads. It reads a line starting "Key learnings:" (or "Lessons:" or "Learned:") followed by the text, or the heading "## Key learnings" with the text under it; a section with no words in it does not count.
 line 3: This commit would contain: {files} (or: This commit records a remote change and contains no files.)
 line 4: Do not run git commit yourself: it skips this check, and improve-complete counts commits made without a lessons section.
3. CITATIONS. message, problems = shiploop_git.resolve_citations(repo, message). If problems:
 line 1: Fix the Learned-from lines in {mp} (delete a line if that commit did not help), then run: {cmd}
 line 2: A citation is one line, "Learned-from: <commit id> <what it contributed>", with 7 to 64 hex digits of a commit reachable from HEAD; ShipLoop writes the full ID into the commit.
 then one line per problem: "- line 7: e1ffd08bd names a commit that is not reachable from HEAD" / "...names no commit in this repository" / "...matches 2 commits (a1b2c3d4e5f6, a1b2c3d4e5f7); write more digits" / "...is not a commit ID (7 to 64 hex digits)" / "line 6: say what the commit contributed after its ID".
 Citations are optional and there is no "none cited" filler line.
4. CREDENTIALS, on the text that will be committed (full IDs included; full 40/64-hex IDs do not trip privacy.sensitive_text, probed). If privacy.sensitive_text(message):
 line 1: Remove the credential-looking text from {mp} and name where it is kept instead, then run: {cmd}
 line 2: ShipLoop screens the commit message for secrets and does not echo the value.
 This replaces today's early _reject_credentials(message, ...) whose first line named neither the file nor the command.
5. COMMIT. If the citations changed any line, write the normalised message back to message_path with store.atomic_write_text (so the committed text equals what was checked), then shiploop_git.commit_paths(repo, pending, "", allow_empty=not pending, message_file=message_path). Success lines: unchanged "Committed this review's changes as {12}: {paths}." and, for no files, "Committed this review's remote change as {12}: it changed no file."; the message file is unlinked on success, the skipped-credential notice and "Nothing committed." branches are unchanged.

Why this order: nothing-to-commit has no side effect and must not demand anything; already-recorded is the same kind of no-op; lessons is the cheapest check and the owner's rule; citations need git; the credential screen runs last on the exact bytes that will be committed.

commit_paths changes (the one commit helper):
- every git commit gets --cleanup=whitespace;
- the allow_empty branch becomes: git commit -q --cleanup=whitespace --allow-empty --only (-F message_file | -m message); the old branch ignored message_file and, without --only, absorbed whatever was staged (both verified, see git_experiments);
- message may be str or a callable taking the paths actually committed (after the credential screen), used by the leftovers commit;
- new helpers: resolve_commit(repo, token) -> (full id, why-not), resolve_citations(repo, message) -> (message with full IDs, [problem lines]), messages_since(repo, base) -> [(id, message)] (non-merge commits reachable from HEAD and not from base; base '' = all).
resolve_commit reads the token with git rev-parse --disambiguate=<hex> (object-name prefixes only, so a branch spelled like hex cannot shadow it, verified), keeps only objects whose git cat-file -t is commit, refuses 0 or more than 1, then git merge-base --is-ancestor <id> HEAD.

improve_changes.commit_refusal(changes, receipt, command="") (command passed down through _improve_change_gate(..., command="") from the improve-complete branch of dispatch) becomes:
 line 1: Commit this review's changes first with improve-commit (write the message to {mp}, then run: {cmd}), then run the same improve-complete command again.
 line 2: ShipLoop Improve import: the review changed these files but did not commit them:
 - path ... (one per line, byte-identical to today so the existing assertion holds)
 last: An Improve review makes the changes it finds warranted, in code, tests or documentation, and commits them through improve-commit: the message needs a "Key learnings:" line, and ShipLoop commits exactly these files. A git commit typed by hand skips that check. If the user or repository said not to commit, add no_commit to the receipt with that instruction.
With command == "" line 1 reads "Commit this review's changes first with the improve-commit command its packet prints, then run the same improve-complete command again."

improve_changes.bind_writes adds a "head" key (git rev-parse --verify -q HEAD; '' on an unborn branch) to the bind snapshot; review_changes ignores it. New improve_changes.window_commits(run_dir, repo, action) -> list[(id, message)] | None (None when the record has no head key, the same fail-open posture as review_changes).

parent-return.md (written by _improve_start, a run file, 0 contract bytes) gains: "Committing a review iteration (the one ShipLoop command the child runs): write the commit message to {mp} with a file-writing tool, then run:\n{cmd}\n- The message needs a line starting \"Key learnings:\" (or the heading \"## Key learnings\") saying what this iteration taught that a later iteration or run should reuse. ShipLoop refuses a commit without it.\n- To credit a commit that helped, add a line \"Learned-from: <commit id> <what it contributed>\". The ID is 7 to 64 hex digits of a commit reachable from HEAD; ShipLoop writes the full ID. A line is optional; delete one rather than guess an ID.\n- To record a change to a remote system that left no file change, add a line \"Remote change: <system alias>, <what changed>, <where its evidence is>\" (no secrets). With no pending file changes ShipLoop then makes a commit with no files; the same text is recorded once.\n- A review that changed no file makes no commit. Never run git commit yourself: it skips these checks, and improve-complete counts such commits."

What a model that reads only line 1 does: each first line carries the label or the action plus the full runnable command, so it edits the file and re-runs (the route tests execute that named command). For citations it will most likely delete the line (optional by design). Risk it can bypass with raw git: counted by the notice, not preventable (hooks are disabled on purpose).
design.script_built_bodies:
All callers of commit_paths (grep of skills/shiploop/scripts): knowledge_home.commit (via navigator._knowledge_close), item_scope.commit_item (via navigator._item_commit), workspace.commit_leftovers, workspace.bootstrap_empty, navigator._improve_commit. Commits not made by commit_paths and left unchanged: the chain merge (git merge --no-ff -m _prepared_message in shiploop_chain_git) and the private baseline (commit-tree), both mechanical.

PRODUCER BODIES (all subjects unchanged):
1. Knowledge commit, every stage in CLOSES (prepare, test-spec, release-plan, release-verify) and every non-close stage that changed the home. New knowledge_home.commit_message(state, stage, rows=()) and commit(state, stage, rows=()); _knowledge_close passes rows = the transition's new history rows. Body = for each done row, "Result (<stage>):" + newline + the accepted summary verbatim, rows separated by a blank line. release-verify keeps its outcome.md sections FIRST with the bytes it has today ("Learned\n...\n\nKey considerations\n...\n\nOpen for the next run\n..."), then the Result block, so the existing pin "knowledge at release-verify\n\nLearned\nlightning__Tab creates no tab." still holds. With rows=() (graph dry-run, existing tests) the message stays subject-only. Real example, run 20261008/r3-battleship-sonnet (state.md history row 3, stage spec):
 docs(shiploop): record build-a-small-single-player-battleship-8f4f83 knowledge after spec
 
 Result (spec):
 Living spec written with R-1..R-10, each with a Confirm-by method. Every request sentence maps: PORT/server (R-1), HTML page titled Battleship with 10x10 grid (R-2), /api/new (R-3), ... NFRs: in-memory state, body cap, no ship leak, no deps (R-9,R-10); ... No pre-existing requirements to preserve.
 (620 characters; lessons section: none). prepare gives 326 characters, release-plan 453, both record-only. release-verify there is 2,025 characters and carries lessons (outcome.md "Learned" bullets) before its Result block.
2. Item (integrate) commit: new item_scope.commit_message(state, row) called from _item_commit. Subject "feat: <id> <title>" unchanged; body = the integrate summary verbatim (as today) + a "Learned:" block when earlier done rows of the same work item (stages before integrate, not integrate itself) have lessons.lessons(summary) non-empty: one line per stage, "- (<stage>) <lesson text collapsed to one line>". On the r3 run (W1) the harvest finds nothing, so the message is today's message byte for byte. See integrate_body_d5.
3. Leftovers commit (workspace.commit_leftovers): message becomes a callable of the committed paths:
 chore(shiploop): commit files written after the last work item, before the return
 
 These files were written after the last work item's commit, so no item commit carries them. ShipLoop commits them here so the return can fast-forward:
 - test/system.test.js
 (saved case: r1-battleship-sonnet 8140857, whose message named no file). Files the credential screen skipped are not listed, because the callable receives the post-screen list.
4. Empty baseline ("Empty baseline for the first ShipLoop run"): stays subject-only; the script holds nothing. Chain merges: unchanged.

WHAT IS NOT LESSONS: a stage summary is a record of what the step established, not what it learned. The script never labels it Learned and never fabricates a lessons line; a commit with no lessons section reads as a plain record ("Result (...)" only), with no filler. The harness counts "with lessons" from the parser, so a body without lessons is counted honestly (the audit's "commits with a body" measure was gameable).

HARVEST RULE for lessons in summaries: the summary is copied verbatim, so any recognised section in it (line-start "Lessons:", "Learned:", "Key learnings:", a heading, a bare label, or an inline label after a sentence end) is found IN PLACE by the same parser; nothing is lifted or rewritten, so there is no duplicate. The one place text is lifted is the item commit's Learned: block (earlier stages of the item). Label to request from the fork: a line starting "Lessons:" or "Learned:" (both read; "Lessons:" also works inline and already appears in saved summaries).

CONSEQUENCE: carry-forward, the stage whose goal is "record lessons", runs AFTER integrate, so its lessons can reach git only through its own knowledge commit (Result block), never the feat commit; the fork should ask carry-forward for the label too.

Not harvested: the Improve --notes text (receipt.lessons), 20 of 205 saved results, successor handoffs that the next packet already prints. Adding it later is one more source in commit_message (a Learned: block, text indented so a nested heading cannot end the section).
design.remote_change:
GRAMMAR: a "Remote change" section in the improve-commit message, forms heading / "Remote change:" line / bare label (no inline), non-empty body; asked content "<system alias>, <what changed>, <where its evidence is>", no secrets, not checked (an evidence locator may dangle; unknowns). No flag, no schema: the section is the trigger (audit finding 10).

EVIDENCE: 0 of 384 saved commits carry one and no local case changes a remote system; the live measure expects 0 empty-diff commits. The first real case is the Salesforce developer-org test on the todo list.

FLOW: pending files empty and a non-empty Remote change section: skip "Nothing to commit"; if an earlier commit since the bind carries the same (whitespace-collapsed) Remote change text, print the no-op "already recorded" line and stop; otherwise require lessons (the owner's "with lessons learned" also covers the empty commit), validate citations and credentials, then commit_paths(repo, [], "", allow_empty=True, message_file=message_path) -> git commit --cleanup=whitespace --allow-empty --only -F <file>. Staged unrelated files stay staged (verified, including an unborn branch and a staged deletion). The message file is unlinked, so re-running without rewriting it is refused by the existing "write the commit message with a file tool first" check; a rewritten identical section is stopped by the guard. With pending files AND a Remote change section the section simply rides in the ordinary file commit.

WHAT THE EMPTY COMMIT LOOKS LIKE (message as the model wrote it; the script adds nothing):
 Record the staging cache purge
 
 Remote change: staging-site, purged the CDN cache after build 41 deployed (evidence: /abs/path/release-check.log)
 Key learnings: the staging host caches index.html for 10 minutes; purge after every deploy.
 Learned-from: 3f2a9c1e0b7d4a5c8e6f1a2b3c4d5e6f708192a3 the release-check log format
 git show --stat HEAD lists no files; git diff --cached still lists the unrelated staged file.

GUARD DEPENDENCY: "since the bind" needs the HEAD recorded at improve-bind (new head key in improve/<action>-bind.md). A child bound by an older build has no key: the guard and the improve-complete notice are skipped (unknown, silent), like review_changes today. That is the only tolerance for an older artifact and it never blocks.

FOLLOW-UP RETURN IN A WORKTREE RUN: follow_up_knowledge_return (shiploop_workspace) returns None when "git diff --name-only <receipt head> HEAD" is empty, so an empty commit made after a return would not be carried automatically. NOT needed now: Improve children run only at spec, test-strategy, plan, step-plan, test-spec, carry-forward (last item), system-test-author and release-plan (shiploop_stage_spec improve attributes), all before the release return; an Improve commit made before the return travels in the fast-forward like any other (and, like every run commit, is lost on the working-tree return route). The follow_up call is also made only for knowledge closes, never for improve-commit. Smallest change when a stage-level remote-change commit is built (deferred; trigger: the first real remote case): in follow_up_knowledge_return replace "if not changed or dirty or not all(in_home)" by "if (not changed and not new_commits) or dirty or not all(in_home)" with new_commits = git rev-list --count <head>..HEAD; plan_return then keeps the prior fast-forward-merge route (_return_kind), so only a fast-forward return carries a no-file commit.

COVERAGE GAP TO STATE PLAINLY: the stage that changes a remote system is release (the deploy), then release-verify and operations; none runs an Improve child. Through improve-commit alone a deploy's lessons reach git only via release-verify's outcome.md commit (the home changed). The stage-level path needs no schema: in knowledge.commit, when the home is unchanged and lessons.remote_change(summary) of a done row is non-empty, make the empty commit with the same grammar (about 15 lines plus the follow-up change above). Deferred per plan 0a.

design.unknowns:
U1 Contract headroom. The pointer (A, +102/+134 bytes) is a guess until spike S measures real-path headroom per stage; fixture figures are 4,422-5,202 bytes of allowance. Resolution: the ladder A+policy -> A -> A0 -> nothing; the engine does not depend on it. Measure improve-start size refusals and the printed allowance in the live pair.
U2 Filler lessons. The gate checks presence only. Saved evidence: 4 of 5 Key learnings in one battleship-1 run restate their Changes text, and one checkers-1 commit says "none new beyond commit ...". Resolution: never refuse on content (no word list, no threshold); the harness records lesson length and whether the lessons text equals the Changes text, descriptively.
U3 False refusals (a refusal costs a turn and invites filler). Legitimate commits that can still be refused once: a bulleted or bold label, a four-hash heading, a different word ("Learnings:", "Takeaways:"), a Learned-from naming a commit on another branch (not reachable from HEAD), a hex-spelled branch or tag name, a shallow clone missing the object. Expected rate from the saved Improve commits: 0 of 42 with the inline form accepted (5 would be refused without it). Every refusal names the accepted forms in line 1-2 and says a Learned-from line may simply be deleted. First-turn refusals are likely on EVERY child until the fork's packet line (lines_for_fork 1) ships with or before the gate; the card already requires Key learnings and 12 of 13 recent commits comply.
U4 Raw-git bypass cannot be prevented (hooks are disabled on purpose; 14 of 20 model-typed commits in the saved runs fell in Improve windows, about 35% of Improve-window commits). The notice prints at improve-complete, after the commits exist, so it can only teach the NEXT child; whether it changes behaviour is unmeasured. Stronger options (refuse improve-complete, amend) were rejected: S-14 and they would require more raw git. Probe: count raw commits per Improve window before and after (fidelity.model_commits plus metrics.commits).
U5 Bind snapshots written by an older build have no head key: the notice and the Remote change guard are silent for such a child. Only affects a run resumed across the release (the E2E harness's --resume-run). Not a state-version change.
U6 Citation uptake. Only 9 of 200 saved commits cite a real earlier SHA, and models cite in free text ("Related commits: a4ce4f1..fd78ab4 ..."), which is not validated. Whether models adopt "Learned-from:" lines is unknown; measure cited and cited_earlier_run in the first pair. Optional by design.
U7 Evidence locator of a Remote change may dangle (not checked). Resolution: the packet asks for a path or URL; revisit with the first real remote case.
U8 The remote-change commit through improve-commit does not cover release, release-verify or operations (no Improve child). Resolution: documented gap; the stage-level path is about 15 lines in knowledge.commit plus the follow_up_knowledge_return change (see remote_change), deferred to the Salesforce case.
U9 follow_up_knowledge_return with an empty commit after a return: analysed, unverified by a run. The route follows _return_kind (a prior fast-forward keeps its route), so only a fast-forward return would carry a no-file commit. Probe when built.
U10 Script bodies repeat summaries (median 302, max 2,502 characters in 1,223 saved rows) in git history; the summaries are already credential-screened at submission. argv: git commit -m with a 300 KB message worked on macOS; Linux limits one argument to 128 KiB. Not observed, no cap invented; if seen, pass the message with -F - (git() would need an input parameter).
U11 Until the fork asks for "Lessons:"/"Learned:" in stage summaries, script commits carry records but almost no new lessons (2 of 1,223 summaries today). Expected baseline for the live pair: script with_lessons about one per finished run (release-verify).
U12 Improve --notes lessons (20 of 205 saved results) are not harvested: they are successor handoffs, the next packet already prints them, and labelling them Learned would overclaim. Probe: classify the 20; if they read as lessons, add one source to commit_message.
U13 Reachability uses HEAD of the execution checkout. In an in-place run where the user commits meanwhile, "commits since the bind" in the notice can include the user's own commits; the wording says "made since this review was bound".
U14 Merge conflicts with the E2E fork: this design edits only these navigator functions: _improve_commit, _improve_start (parent-return.md text), improve_start_contract (authority string), _improve_change_gate, the improve-complete branch of dispatch, _item_commit, _knowledge_close; and in knowledge_home only commit/commit_message/learnings and the _sections removal (not stage_lines or recent_commits, which the fork owns).
U15 The newest saved run (20261010/battleship-1) writes labels in one paragraph and checkers-1 on separate lines: the model's habit varies by session, which is why both forms are accepted.

design.build_order:
Nine small commits, each independently green (suites in footprint_suites). Change-note policy: commits 1-2 carry "No-Change-Note: internal helper, no installed behaviour change" (commit 2's --cleanup flag only matters with a user commit.cleanup setting); commit 3 creates changes/shiploop/commit-lessons-and-citations.md (bump: minor) and later commits amend the same note. No commit edits skills/improve/**, plugins/, versions or CHANGELOG, and none changes STATE_VERSION (4).
1. shiploop_lessons.py + knowledge_home.learnings() on it (delete _sections) + the five LessonsGrammarTests and test_release_verify_learnings_come_from_the_shared_parser. Pure; fail-first = ImportError.
2. shiploop_git: --cleanup=whitespace everywhere, the empty commit with --allow-empty --only honouring message_file, callable message, resolve_commit, resolve_citations, messages_since; the CommitHelperTests above. The bootstrap_empty caller and existing helper tests stay green.
3. improve_changes: head in the bind snapshot, window_commits, commit_refusal(command); navigator._improve_change_gate(command=) from the improve-complete branch; tests; state-files.md row. First visible change, so the change note starts here.
4. _improve_commit: new order (nothing-to-commit, lessons, citations, credentials), refusal texts, message rewrite, parent-return.md paragraph in _improve_start; update the existing test_improve_commit_commits_only_the_reviews_uncommitted_changes message (it has no Key learnings and would now be refused); CLI tests for lessons, order, citations, inline form, strip cleanup, parent-return route, planning child.
5. Remote change: empty-delta path and the already-recorded guard (depends on 3 and 4) and its tests.
6. improve-complete notice (depends on 3): compute the window BEFORE save/_knowledge_close so the script's own knowledge commit is not counted, print after save; tests.
7. Script-built bodies: knowledge_home.commit_message / commit(rows), _knowledge_close passes rows, item_scope.commit_message and _item_commit, workspace.commit_leftovers callable message; tests; project-knowledge.md paragraph. Independent of 3-6.
8. Contract text per spike S: authority pointer (A+policy, A, A0 or none) with its pin test; text-only and droppable; must follow commit 4 so the pointer is true.
9. Docs, journal and evidence: SKILL.md two sentences, improve-context.md, journal entry with the forms scan, the baseline regrade (script 292/26, non-script by script identity 67/44, model-typed 25/2), the git experiment outputs and byte counts under docs/experiments/commit-contract-engine-<date>/.
Order versus the E2E fork: commits 1, 2, 5 (git part), 7 touch no fork-owned function; 3, 4, 6, 8 touch the navigator functions listed in unknowns U14, so rebase them after the fork's release A merges. Release: one minor release for the series (plan row B), after the harness counters (task H) exist so a baseline is regraded first.
design.complete_notice:
improve-complete prints one line on STDOUT (like the other ShipLoop notices, so the harness sees it in tool output), after the import is saved, before the next packet, only on the first successful import of a child.

READS: improve/<action>-bind.md key "head" (the HEAD recorded at improve-bind) and git log --no-merges <head>..HEAD via shiploop_git.messages_since; counts the commits whose message has no lessons section (shiploop_lessons.lessons(message) is ''). The window is computed before save and the knowledge close, so the script's own knowledge commit is not counted.

WORDING (stable prefix for the harness):
ShipLoop Improve notice: {k} of {n} commits made since this review was bound carry no lessons section ({id12}, {id12}). They did not go through improve-commit, which needs a "Key learnings:" line. Nothing was refused; commit the next review's changes with the improve-commit command its packet prints.

SILENT when: n is 0 or k is 0; the improve-complete is a replay (no second import); the receipt carries no_commit; the bind record has no head key (unknown). Never a refusal and never waits on a person (S-14). It counts bypass; it cannot prevent it.

design.git_experiments:
All in temp repositories under the scratchpad (git 2.54.0 Apple Git-157). Scripts: exp/*.py and the shell blocks reproduced here.
E1 empty commit with an unrelated staged file: "git commit -q --allow-empty --only -F msg.md" -> exit 0, "git show --name-only" lists no file, "git status --porcelain" still shows "A  staged.txt", the "## Key learnings" and "## Remote change" headings are stored. The same call WITHOUT --only ("git commit -q --allow-empty -m ...", what commit_paths does today) listed "staged.txt" inside the empty commit: it absorbs the index.
E2 cleanup. No config, -F: headings kept, trailing blanks stripped. commit.cleanup=strip, -F or -m, no flag: the stored message LOST its "## Key learnings" and "## Remote change" lines (body read "- one" and "- staging-site: purged cache" only). commit.cleanup=strip plus --cleanup=whitespace: headings kept. scissors: kept. verbatim: trailing blanks kept, and --cleanup=whitespace normalises them. So --cleanup=whitespace is required for Markdown "#" headings whenever a user config sets strip; the flag overrides config.
E3 unborn branch: "git commit --allow-empty --only -m" works (empty tree, bootstrap_empty unaffected, tested with no identity configured: author "ShipLoop Workspace"); with a staged file the file stays staged; a staged deletion stays staged ("D  z.txt"); an unstaged tracked edit stays unstaged. "git commit --only -m x" with no paths and no --allow-empty fails: "fatal: No paths with --include/--only does not make sense." (exit 128), so the flag pair matters.
E4 citation resolution: "git rev-parse --disambiguate=<7 hex>" prints the full ID of every object with that prefix (empty output and exit 0 when none); "git rev-parse --verify <hex>^{commit}" resolves a BRANCH named cafe123 (shadowing) while --disambiguate does not; a tree ID is listed by --disambiguate and rejected by "git cat-file -t" (tree); "git merge-base --is-ancestor <id> HEAD" returns 0 for HEAD and the root commit and 1 for a commit on another branch. A real 7-digit prefix collision cannot be built, so the ambiguous case is tested with the rev-parse output mocked. Prototype run over a 31-commit repo with commit.cleanup=strip configured: a good prefix was rewritten to the 40-hex ID, an unreachable one, a non-hex token and a blank contribution each produced one problem line; the empty commit kept both headings; messages_since(base) listed the three commits after base plus the empty one, messages_since('') listed all 31.
E5 argv size: git commit -m with a 300 KB message and -F - with 300 KB both succeeded on macOS (ARG_MAX 1,048,576); Linux limits a single argument to 128 KiB (not run here).
E6 privacy screen: privacy.sensitive_text is False for a line with a 40-hex or a 64-hex commit ID, so full IDs in Learned-from lines do not trip the credential refusal.
Also read-only data scans (exp/scan_forms.py, run_proto.py, baseline.py, scan_states.py, scan_notes.py, scan_summ.py, contract_bytes.py, option_bytes2.py) produced the figures quoted in the other fields.

Limits stated honestly: carry-forward, the stage that records lessons, runs after integrate, so its lessons reach git through its own knowledge commit ("after carry-forward"), not the feat commit; and no engine notice is printed at integrate (it would be post-hoc and always on until adoption): the harness counts script commits with lessons instead.

CLAUSES TOUCHED: S-5 (SHAs resolved by git, bodies built by the script, the model supplies only the message), S-6 and the main tenet (every refusal restates its fix and exact command in line 1; the command and rules sit in parent-return.md, a file the frozen contract names, so a cleared child can recover; the route tests execute the named command), S-12 (one grammar module, one commit helper; knowledge_home._sections removed; empty commits go through commit_paths; no second credential screen), S-14 (no new prompt; every refusal is fixable by the model; the improve-complete notice never refuses; nothing waits on stdin), S-7 (engine adds 0 packet bytes; frozen contract +102 to +134 bytes depending on spike S; parent-return.md grows by about 1.1 KB as a run file), S-11 (commit messages are part of the retained knowledge; the knowledge-home commits still commit exactly docs/shiploop/ and SHIPLOOP.md), S-4 (no new verb or flag; improve-commit keeps its arguments). S-9 is respected: a lessons section is never offered as evidence of anything.

NON-REGRESSION STATEMENT: unchanged byte for byte: the "Nothing to commit" path and its text (and it never asks for lessons, D4); which files a commit stages (exactly the review's pending paths); the credential screen per file and its skipped-file notice; every script commit subject; the release-verify body (outcome.md sections first); the Improve card, packets and stage_lines (not edited here); STATE_VERSION 4 and every state key; no trailers; stage results and their keys; improve-complete never refuses over lessons; the no_commit receipt route; hooks stay disabled. Changed on purpose: improve-commit refuses a commit message with no lessons section or with a bad Learned-from line; its credential refusal now names the file and command; commit_refusal names improve-commit; commits use --cleanup=whitespace (a fix for users with commit.cleanup=strip); an empty remote-change commit becomes possible; script commits gain bodies. Saved runs: no state refusal; only a child bound by an older build loses the head-based notice and guard.

LIVE PAIR MEASURES (with the task-H counters metrics.commits = {improve:{n, with_lessons, cited, cited_earlier_run}, script:{n, with_lessons}}, same case and host as the previous baseline row, no thresholds; unmeasured stays unknown): (1) refusals by first line, bucketed on these fixed prefixes: "Add a \"Key learnings:\" line to", "Fix the Learned-from lines in", "Remove the credential-looking text from", "Commit this review's changes first with improve-commit", "write the commit message with a file tool first", and whether the same first line repeated; (2) improve commits with lessons (expect n by construction) versus bypasses (fidelity.model_commits inside Improve windows; the count of "ShipLoop Improve notice:" lines); (3) citations: Learned-from lines per run and how many name a commit from before the run's baseline; (4) script commits with lessons (baseline from the regrade: script 292 commits of which 26 carry lessons, about one per finished run; non-script commits by a script identity 67 of which 44; model-typed 25 of which 2); (5) descriptive lesson length and whether the lessons text equals the Changes text; (6) empty-diff commits (expect 0 locally); (7) improve-start size refusals and the printed opening allowance (contract cost); (8) packet bytes (expect unchanged from the engine) and turns spent after each new refusal. audits.verdict: Do not build as written; build a smaller version. The core is sound and I reproduced its git claims in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-dadleet-src-skill-craft/f24838dd-d5f5-44a8-854e-3d9ddea18aed/scratchpad/audit-yagni (git 2.54). First, `git commit --allow-empty --only -F` leaves an unrelated staged file staged, and without `--only` the empty commit absorbs it. Second, `commit.cleanup=strip` deletes `## Key learnings` and `## Remote change` lines, and `--cleanup=whitespace` restores them. Third, `rev-parse --disambiguate` is not shadowed by a branch named like the prefix, while `--verify <hex>^{commit}` is. Fourth, `--is-ancestor` works on a detached HEAD. The DEFAULT_COMMIT_AUTHORITY pins are indeed hand-written fixtures, and the +102 byte authority delta recomputes exactly. Four things need fixing before any code. (1) Two parts break fixed constraints: `Remote change: none` breaks D4, and the `head` fallback for old bind records breaks "one supported version". (2) The grammar refuses real lessons in two plausible layouts. (3) The claim that the engine adds 0 packet bytes is false for intake and discovery. (4) About half the surface fails YAGNI: no saved run shows the failure it fixes, or its benefit cannot be seen until fork-owned packet text ships. All 42 saved Improve-style commits already carry Key learnings, so the improve-commit lessons gate has almost no compliance upside; its value is the owner's rule and the metric. That makes every false refusal pure cost.

blockers.claim: A Remote change section that says nothing remote happened ('Remote change: none', 'n/a') breaks D4: it makes an empty commit, or demands lessons from a no-change review.
blockers.evidence: The design's has_content rule counts any letter or digit. In the prototype, remote_change('Remote change: none') returns 'none' and remote_change('Remote change: n/a - nothing deployed') is non-empty. In _improve_commit, `not pending and not remote` is the only route to 'Nothing to commit'. So a review that changed no file but whose message fills a 'Remote change: none' label (Luna and Grok fill every labelled section; the card lists six) skips that no-op. It then either commits an empty commit, or is refused for missing lessons. Both break fixed constraint (f): a pass that changes nothing makes no commit and never asks for lessons.
blockers.fix: Keep Remote change detection structural, not a word list: the body must hold the asked-for three fields (alias, change, evidence). If the section is present but does not, refuse once with the exact format and 'delete the line when nothing remote changed'. Never fall through to an empty commit. Better still, defer the whole empty-commit path (see cuts).

blockers.claim: The bind `head` key tolerates old artifacts: window_commits returns None when the key is missing, and the already-recorded guard and the improve-complete notice are then skipped silently (U5; second assertion of test_the_same_remote_change_is_recorded_once).
blockers.evidence: The fixed constraints say one supported version: no compat shims, fallbacks or migrations, refuse old artifacts by name. The design calls this 'the only tolerance for an older artifact', which is exactly the forbidden fallback. A run resumed across the release (the harness's --resume-run) hits it.
blockers.fix: Drop the dependency. Cut the notice and keep no bind change. Implement the duplicate guard with a per-action marker in the run directory (for example improve/<action>-remote.md holding the whitespace-collapsed Remote change text), or compare against the HEAD message. A missing marker means 'not recorded yet', which is a fact, not a fallback. If head is kept, refuse by name when it is absent.

corrections.claim: The grammar claims 'colon then prose on the next line' is read. It is not read when a blank line follows the label, or when the first body line looks like 'Word: text'. A legitimate commit with real lessons is then refused.
corrections.evidence:
Prototype probes. 'Key learnings:

- a thing' returns ''. 'Key learnings:
Pitfall: board is 0-based' returns ''. The bare form 'Key learnings

Decision: x' also returns ''. Cause: the body stops at a blank line, and at any `Word(s):` line (_LABEL_LINE), including the first line. The Luna fixture (test/fixtures/fidelity/v1210-battleship-luna-xhigh) writes bare labels on their own line through a heredoc, so a label-alone layout is real. Today's Key learnings text is always inline (35 of 37 followed by another label), so the saved data never exercised this. The same parser grades the harness, so it would also undercount.
corrections.fix: Stop only at known section labels (Review, Plan, Changes, Validation, Key learnings/Lessons/Learned, Remaining work, Remote change, Learned-from, Co-Authored-By, Signed-off-by). When the label line has no text, skip blank lines and take the first non-blank line unless it is a known label, heading or fence. I prototyped this as scratchpad/audit-yagni/lessons_fixed.py. The previously refused cases now pass, 'Key learnings:\nRemaining work: x' stays empty, and the saved-history count stays 72 of 384.

corrections.claim: 'The engine adds 0 packet bytes' (spec_admission S-7, footprint_suites) is false for intake and discovery.
corrections.evidence: knowledge_home.stage_lines prints recent_commits(repo) for those two stages. That is `git log -3 --format=%h %B`, the last three full messages with no truncation. Result blocks append the accepted summary to every knowledge commit. In the saved r3-battleship-sonnet state.md the last eight stage summaries are 214 to 877 characters (max 1,225, and 2,502 across the saved set). The next run's intake therefore grows by roughly the sum of the last three Result blocks. That is the packet area the fork is compacting and shiploop-packet-bounds covers.
corrections.fix: State the cost. Preferably replace Result blocks with a lessons-only harvest (see cuts), so only commits that actually carry lessons grow the quoted text.

corrections.claim: A Learned-from token must match 7 to 64 hex digits exactly, so common model spellings are refused as 'not a commit ID'.
corrections.evidence: Tokens are the first whitespace-delimited word. A backticked id, 'abc1234:', '[abc1234]', and 'commit abc1234' all fail the regex. I confirmed that `rev-parse --disambiguate` returns nothing for the backticked and colon forms. Uppercase hex does resolve. Citation is the owner's requirement (1), and the refusal's cheapest exit for a model is to delete the line, which loses it.
corrections.fix: Strip surrounding backticks, quotes, brackets, parentheses and trailing colon/comma/period from the token, and skip a leading 'commit', before the hex check.

corrections.claim: Replacing knowledge_home._sections with the shared parser leaves outcome.md reading behaviour unchanged.
corrections.evidence: The old parser read headings only. The shared one also matches colon, bare and inline labels anywhere outside a wanted heading (a 'Learned: x' line in a preamble or another section becomes a second 'Learned'), and skips fences. has_content makes '## Learned\n-' empty where the old release-verify gate accepted it. It is unspecified which duplicate wins in the dict that learnings() builds.
corrections.fix: Have learnings() request the heading form only, or define first-wins, and add a test. Name the has_content tightening as an intended change.

corrections.claim: The label set is narrower than the layouts the design accepts, so plain-English variants are refused.
corrections.evidence: Probes: 'Learnings:', 'Lesson:', 'Takeaways:', '**Key learnings:** x', '- Key learnings: x' and 'Key learnings (this pass): x' all return ''. Yet the one-paragraph inline form is accepted to save 5 of 42 saved commits, all from one run (battleship-1).
corrections.fix: Add 'Learnings', 'Learning' and 'Lesson' to LESSON_LABELS. Either tolerate an optional '- ' or '**' prefix, or drop the inline form. The design currently takes the leniency that is less likely and refuses the more likely.

corrections.claim: The lessons refusal invites filler, and the design records 'none' as a lesson.
corrections.evidence: The gate accepts any text with a letter. Saved examples are r3-battleship-sonnet 7e11860 ('the quality loop traced server entry points; the page's async state needed the same scrutiny') and checkers-1 ('none new beyond commit ...'). A trivial iteration (a typo fix) has nothing to teach, and the refusal gives no honest exit. has_content counts 'none', so harness with_lessons is inflated.
corrections.fix: Say in line 2: 'if the iteration taught nothing new, write Key learnings: none; do not invent a lesson'. Have the harness record the lesson text, so honest 'none' can be separated afterwards. That is descriptive, not a word list in the gate.

corrections.claim: Option A (+102 bytes) is recommended, but the authority string keeps 'the selected Improve card's scoped-commit policy' next to the new pointer.
corrections.evidence: The card's Commit policy tells the child to use `git commit --only -- <paths>`. That is the likely cause of the 35% bypass, and the contract still sends the child to it. Refusal line 1 already restates the 'Key learnings' rule on first use, so the 71 extra bytes over A0 are redundant.
corrections.fix: Default to A0 (+31) plus the parent-return.md rules. Reword the commit-policy clause itself to 'commit only with improve-commit (see P), not git commit'. Drop the 'no empty commit except a recorded remote change' clause (+32) unless the remote path ships.

corrections.claim: D5 'harvest earlier same-item summaries into the feat commit' has no supporting case and cannot receive the only observed labelled summaries.
corrections.evidence: The integrate summary is already the commit body today, so the brief's 'lessons from its result' is met when the fork asks integrate for the label. Only 2 of 1,223 saved summaries carry a label, and both are carry-forward, which runs after integrate (stage_spec order), so it can never feed a feat: commit. The r3 W1 harvest finds nothing (0 of 35).
corrections.fix: Make the engine side of D5 empty for now: no item_scope.commit_message. Count with the parser, and add the harvest when counted runs show earlier-stage labels.

corrections.claim: The improve-complete notice reaches the wrong reader and can blame the wrong author.
corrections.evidence: The frozen contract says the parent runs improve-complete. The raw commits are the child's, and the stdout notice prints after they exist. The design admits it can only teach the NEXT child (U4) and that in-place runs count the user's own commits (U13). The harness already measures this: fidelity.model_commits plus metrics.commits improve {n, with_lessons} gives the bypass count from the same parser.
corrections.fix: Cut it (see cuts).

corrections.claim: Two listed tests cannot fail: test_the_planning_child_can_commit_through_improve_commit, and the 'passes today' D4 test as a fail-first test.
corrections.evidence: improve-commit is dispatched by verb, not gated on packet text, so the planning-child test passes before and after; its own fails_when is hedged ('if the command were route-gated'). The D4 test is a regression guard that passes today.
corrections.fix: Drop the first. Keep the D4 test but label it a guard, not fail-first. Instead test that the command printed in parent-return.md is executed and commits (already in the authority test).

cuts.part: improve-complete notice, the bind `head` key, improve_changes.window_commits and shiploop_git.messages_since

Old binds force the forbidden fallback. The harness already counts the bypass from the same parser. Reintroduce only if the first live pair shows the harness count is not enough.

It repeats state.md in git, grows the three messages intake and discovery quote, and mixes absolute run paths into history that a fast-forward return can put on the user's branch. Smaller: append only the lessons section found in the summary, labelled 'Lessons:', when one exists. Subject-only stays otherwise, which constraint (c) allows because the script then holds no lesson. No observed case, and the only labelled summaries run after integrate. See corrections.

Neither fixes an observed failure. Line-anchored plus the known-label stop set covers the saved data (72 of 384).

cuts.why: Redundant with refusal line 1 and parent-return.md.

audits.missed:

Still refused, to fix: label alone then blank line or 'Word:' first line; backticked, colon or 'commit'-prefixed Learned-from tokens; 'Learnings:', 'Lesson:', 'Takeaways:'; bulleted, bold, indented or qualified labels; a lone ``` earlier in the message; 'Remote change: none' (wrong direction, see blockers). Not a problem: CRLF (read_text normalises, and --cleanup=whitespace strips \r in the stored message: verified); label case (matched case-insensitively); no Git (improve-commit already refuses without a bind snapshot, nothing new); detached HEAD (merge-base --is-ancestor exit 0); shallow clone (a commit outside the boundary reports 'names no commit', rare); unborn HEAD (is-ancestor exits 128, the reason says not reachable); non-English headings (the label must be English, content may be any language, and the refusal names the labels). The existing credential screen flags legitimate lesson text. privacy.sensitive_text is True for 'Key learnings: the Bearer token header must be set' and 'set the secret: in config.yml under auth.secret: <alias>'. The screen already runs today, but the new refusal text should say rewording is the fix, not removal of the lesson.
It is unclear whether multiple failing checks should refuse one at a time (up to three turns) or together.
The 35% bypass is the real lever and the gate does not touch it: the authority clause plus parent-return.md plus commit_refusal naming improve-commit are the only parts that do. They should land first and alone.
The design says nothing about the card's own `git commit --only` text and the authority clause that sends the child to it; both belong in lines_for_fork.
Minor: _COLON backtracks quadratically on a line with a long run of spaces (20,000 spaces took 1.2 s); with_full_ids rejoins on \n after splitlines, which also splits at \u2028 and \x0c.
audits.safer_alternative: Ship the smallest change that fixes the observed bypass and meets the owner's explicit rules, in this order, each independently green. (1) shiploop_lessons.py as a leaf module with three line-anchored forms (heading, colon, bare). Include the known-label stop set, the label-alone-then-body rule, 'Learnings'/'Lesson' labels, case-insensitive matching, and no inline form or fence state. learnings() reads headings only. Every refusal's line 1 is the fix plus the exact command, and the route tests run that command. (4) improve_changes.commit_refusal names improve-commit, and parent-return.md gets the rules. The authority becomes A0 (+31 bytes) with the commit-policy clause reworded; this is the bypass fix. No bind change, no notice.
